what: Cameco is one of the world's largest uranium producers. It mines uranium in Canada and Kazakhstan, converts and fabricates nuclear fuel, and owns 49% of Westinghouse, which services and builds nuclear reactors.
customers: Nuclear utilities worldwide, which buy uranium and fuel services under long-term contracts.
money: production from Cigar Lake, McArthur River and the Inkai joint venture
reactor servicing, fuel and new-build engineering, held at 49%
moat: High-grade Canadian uranium deposits that are among the richest in the world, plus Western supply at a time when utilities want to avoid Russian material.
risks: Uranium prices are volatile and the market is thin
Kazakh joint venture production depends on a politically complex partner
Net margin and returns are modest relative to the share price
The shares trade at a very high multiple of current earnings
opportunities: Revenue grew about 17% last year and about 23% a year over three years
Analysts see large upside, with a median target well above the current price
Reactor life extensions, restarts and new builds are all adding to long-term uranium demand
watch: Contracted uranium volumes and prices, and Westinghouse earnings.
